turns.en: Our competitive advantages are organizational EQ. It's not to dismiss the IQ half of the equation where very bright people think carefully about investment theses.
turns.zh: 我们的竞争优势在于组织的 EQ（情商）。这并非否定 IQ 那一半：非常聪明的人在认真思考投资论点。

turns.en: Our advantages are ultimately in the trust, the relationship, the standing, the patience, patience, and the state and Christensen law of conservation of attractive profits.
turns.zh: 我们的优势最终在信任、关系、声誉、耐心——耐心，以及 Clayton Christensen 的吸引力利润守恒定律。

turns.en: When one part of the value chain is attacked, then value accrues to the adjacent parts of the value chain. If IQ is under attack, value is going to accrue to EQ.
turns.zh: 当价值链的一环被冲击时，价值会流向价值链相邻的环节。如果 IQ 在被冲击，价值就会流向 EQ。

turns.en: Whilst it's really important we are forward on the use of the technology, one of the things all organizations have to do is work out, are they really competing on the IQ side or are they competing on the EQ side?
turns.zh: 所以，虽然我们在技术应用上走在前面非常重要，但每个组织都必须想清楚：我们到底是在 IQ 一侧竞争，还是在 EQ 一侧竞争？

turns.en: Lots of our partners compete on the IQ side. They're leaning heavily into the technology. They are leaning appropriately heavily into it, but I hope with an understanding that what we do brilliantly might not be to become the next smartest investor, but make sure we continue to work with the smartest and best investors in the smartest and best way.
turns.zh: 我们很多伙伴在 IQ 一侧竞争，他们大力投入技术，投入得也合理，但我希望他们明白：我们做得最出色之事不是成为最聪明的投资者，而是确保我们继续以最聪明的方式、与最聪明最优秀的投资者合作。

turns.en: What are some of the things you have tried using the LLMs that haven't been as effective as you would have thought today? If you roll back three years, I would have looked at the machinery as a way of bringing many different challenge perspectives to a problem.
turns.zh: 你试过哪些用 LLM 但效果不如预期的事？往前回看三年，我会把这套机器看成给一个问题引入许多不同质疑视角的方式。

turns.en: The more ways you can challenge a problem, the more ways you can find insights that others haven't thought about. I don't think that's been true.
turns.zh: 你质疑问题的角度越多，就越可能发现别人没想到的洞见。我觉得这一点并不成立。

turns.en: You've got to be far more deliberate about what are the lenses you want to bring to a problem? How do you codify those lenses? How do you make those lenses consistent across the organization?
turns.zh: 你必须更有意识地想：你到底要带哪些视角来看这个问题？怎么把这些视角规则化？怎么让它们在组织内保持一致？

turns.en: The machinery and the platforms haven't caught up with doing that well at this point in time. What are some of the risks you've encountered?
turns.zh: 现阶段机器和平台还没发展到能很好地支撑这一点。你们遇到过哪些风险？

turns.en: The big risk is that we put a lot of effort into this and it does not make us a better investor. That's the one we're focused on most, continuing to push ourselves to understand how we can judge whether we are making better investment decisions.
turns.zh: 最大的风险是，我们投入大量精力，结果它并没有让我们成为更好的投资者。这是我们最聚焦的问题——不断逼自己去理解：怎么判断我们确实做出了更好的投资决策。

turns.en: It's still early in the technological revolution. We are getting to the point in the next 12 to 80 months where you've got to feel confident that you are getting a return on investment of the technology.
turns.zh: 这场技术革命还早。接下来 12 到 18 个月，你会走到必须确信自己从这项技术上拿到了投资回报的阶段。

turns.en: In our case, that means we can really feel confident we are making substantially better investment decisions commensurate with the investment we're putting into it.
turns.zh: 对我们来说，那意味着要真正确信：我们做出了与投入相称的、显著更好的投资决策。

turns.en: The areas I've outlined earlier, those people feel confident are real, benefits real opportunities now. The test case is always in a long-term investment opportunity which might play out over seven years.
turns.zh: 我之前讲的那些领域，大家相信那里的收益是真实的、机会就在眼前。真正的考验永远是那些可能要七年才会兑现的长期投资机会。

turns.en: How do you know that it's helping you make a better decision that turns into a better outcome? We do need to figure it out. Thanks for listening all the way to the end.
turns.zh: 你怎么知道它在帮你做出更好的决策、并最终变成更好的结果？我们确实还需要搞明白。谢谢大家一路听到这里。

turns.en: If you made it this far, how about one ask from me. Tell one friend about the show. It's the best way to keep growing this incredible community.
turns.zh: 如果你听到了最后，我有一个不情之请：把你的一个朋友介绍给我们。这是让这个了不起的社区成长最好的方式。

turns.en: Thanks so much. But until the next one, stay curious and keep compounding knowledge, relationships, and capital a little bit at a time. All opinions expressed by TED and podcast guests are solely their own opinions and do not reflect the opinion of capital allocators or their firms.
turns.zh: 非常感谢。在下一期之前，保持好奇，持续让知识、关系和资本一点点复利增长。Ted 和播客嘉宾表达的所有观点仅为个人观点，不代表 Capital Allocators 或其所在机构的立场。
